content: RTF1, also known as Rtf1, is a protein in humans encoded by the RTF1 gene. This gene is thought to play a role in the regulation of transcription elongation and chromatin remodeling, based on research conducted on similar proteins in other organisms. The protein encoded by this gene may have the ability to bind to single-stranded DNA. To study the function of RTF1, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line named Rtf1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative designed to produce and distribute animal models of human diseases for research purposes. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized series of phenotypic tests to assess the effects of the gene deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and three significant abnormalities were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, indicating that they did not survive to the weaning stage. The remaining tests were therefore performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice. Among these, vertebral fusion was observed specifically in male animals.
